concerns.text: FR‑018 “perform a priori power analysis before any training” is only addressed by the fallback task T014; there is no primary task that runs a power analysis on the full training set (≥ 20 000 molecules) and aborts if power < 0.8, violating the dependency that the power‑analysis producer must precede any training tasks (T005, T007, etc.).

FR‑026 requires title‑token overlap ≥ 0.7 for external citations, but T001 only checks URL accessibility and SHA‑256 checksum; it does not perform the required citation‑title similarity verification, leaving a missing producer for this requirement.

FR‑025 “CI job orchestration (each job ≤ 6 h, ≤ 7 GB RAM)” is not mapped to any concrete task; no task creates or validates the GitHub Actions workflow that enforces the per‑job time and memory limits, breaking the producer‑consumer ordering for the orchestration artifact.

SC‑001 “MAE reduction ≥ 0.05 eV relative to the fingerprint baseline and paired‑test p < 0.05” has no implementing task or verification step; after T010 the plan never computes the GNN‑vs‑baseline MAE difference nor asserts the statistical significance, so the consumer of this metric is missing.

SC‑002 demands reporting Cohen’s d and checking that the MAE increase from ablation is ≥ 0.05 eV; the ablation_result.schema.yaml lacks a Cohen’s d field and no task (e.g., after T007) computes or validates this effect‑size, leaving a missing producer for the required metric.

T009 attribution generation relies on a qualitative “chemical intuition” check without a measurable success criterion, making the outcome untestable; a quantitative validation (e.g., correlation with known Hammett σ values or a defined pass/fail threshold) should be added.
